newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk leads Russian shares up in nervous trading.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk leads Russian shares up in nervous trading.

text.p: Norilsk Nickel pushed the Russian share index up on Wednesday in nervous trading and some dealers said the market was fearing a serious correction after recent strong gains.
Others said the market rise further as investors with uninvested funds hunted for stock to buy.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares rose by 2.87 percent to 503.37 on $82.67 million total market turnover.
Norilsk Nickel metals group was the gain-leader of the day with ordinaries soaring to $13.00 from $11.65. Preferred shares rose to $10.60 from $9.20.
Traders said the share rose ahead of an auction for 38 percent of shares in the plant, bids for which will be taken from July 22 to August 1. Results will be announced on August 5.
Shares have been rising strongly in the next few days and some traders said stocks were overheated.

Irkutskenergo power utility rose to $0.37 from $0.365, Rostelekom was unchanged at $9.41, UES EESR.RTS power utility was up to $0.4690 from $0.4687 and Mosenergo MSNG.RTS power utility edged down to $1.616 from $1.625.
"The market will be nervous in the next few days," said MFK-Renaissance trader Vladimir Chkhikvadze. "If traders sense big sellers it will cause a snowball effect since everyone is scared of a fall."
Rinaco-Plus trader Alexei Rozhkov said the market was not overheated and forecast a further rise in the next few days.
"We are optimistic," he said. "There is a lot of money turning over on the market. Investors will not wait to buy at lower prices as many of them are trying to jump on the bandwagon."

He said there was still a lot of money on the market from Western operators who had turned their assets into cash before the U.S. Federal Reserve Federal Open Market Committee sitting on interest rates last week.
Traders said Russian operators were already taking profits, but since the volumes were small, the market digested them easily.
Healthy 1996 results announced by Uralsvyazinform on Wednesday had no impact on the market as traders thought the price too high. Uralsvyazinform closed at $0.049 on July 8, when it was last traded.
